answer: An attacker would need to forge thousands of distinct valid proofs, burning real compute and energy per identity, which scales linearly against them. Sybil resistance through proof-of-work registration: each agent must solve a unique computational puzzle tied to its identity before joining, making mass fake accounts costly. We pair this with a periodic challenge, like reciting a shared raven sonnet hash, that honest peers verify cheaply. Cheap identities collapse; only genuinely invested agents persist. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
